_comment: The DISCRIMINATION pilot declaration for skillc#287 (orchestrator review, comment 6025311708, decisions P1-P6). Exploratory only: estimates p_hat_intact and p_hat_degraded for evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's choose_n() - draws NO verdict (operator ruling, comment 6021089903). Uses the 'discrimination-declaration' kind added to skillc.calibration by the separate calibration.py PR (branch feat-skillc-287-discrimination-declaration, Refs #287) - see that PR for why skillc.calibration.parse_declaration structurally cannot express this contrast, and _resolution_note below for what changed here as a result.
_resolution_note: This file previously carried kind 'discrimination-pilot-declaration' (not validated by skillc.calibration) with a _schema_note flagging the gap to the orchestrator. Ruling received (orchestrator review, 2026-10-06): add a real 'discrimination-declaration' kind to skillc.calibration instead of accounting this test purely through skillc#273's case-pairing records. This file now uses that kind: arms.degraded.subject.revision is the DERIVED label skillc.calibration._expected_degraded_revision computes (never typed), and arms.degraded.mutation carries the structured mutation (skill/path/removed_text/diagnose_evidence/mutated_digest) the schema requires. case-pairing (skillc#273) still produces the per-attempt record this study's counts read; the declaration-level identity/approval binding is now calibration.py's job, not case-pairing's.

pilot.purpose: exploratory - estimates p_hat_intact and p_hat_degraded for evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's choose_n(); draws no verdict
pilot.no_verdict_statement: This pilot draws no DISCRIMINATING / NOT_SHOWN / UNKNOWN verdict. Its 10 attempts per arm are too few to be the predeclared discrimination test itself (that test is the MAIN study's schedule, sized by this pilot's results) and are never pooled into the main study's counts (P1).
rule_citations: P1 (comment 6025311708): pilot attempts never count toward the main study.

P2 (comment 6025311708): the pilot uses the same two-declaration shape, one pilot declaration per test, each 2-arm at n=10, each separately approved at 10. The intact arm therefore runs in both pilot declarations (see pilot-improvement-declaration.json's 'intact' arm, same subject).

P3 (comment 6025311708): this pilot's own raw proportions (passes/evaluable) must never be plugged into the sizing simulation directly - convert with evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's jeffreys_estimate() first.
P5 (comment 6025311708): tolerance is max(1, ceil(0.05*n)) per arm, not a flat 1.

P6 (comment 6025311708): arm order is calibration's seed-derived interleaving, so the two arms run interleaved in time rather than as two blocks - skillc.calibration.derive_arm_order, called by skillc.calibration.parse_discrimination_declaration itself now, not merely reused as an external scheduling utility.

arms.treatment: the same subject as 'intact' with the mutation below applied, no other installed skill or helper carrying equivalent content (per mutation.diagnose_evidence). removed_text is the exact, verified-single-occurrence substring of codex/skills/flow-check/reference.md at the ea6dbfa pin - read from tests/fixtures/profile-cpp-codex-flow-check-ea6dbfa/codex/skills/flow-check/reference.md (this repository's own committed capture of that file; confirmed byte-for-byte identical to claude-power-pack's own git blob 95995556f1454200a0121670afd1fd6153a3d191 and to the sha256 evals/subjects/cpp-codex-flow-check-ea6dbfa/evidence/inventory.json records for it - not assumed); mutated_digest is sha256 of that file's bytes with removed_text removed once, computed directly from the fixture. Both are re-verified against the REAL claude-power-pack checkout before any live attempt (see owed_before_run) - evals/calibration-287/evidence/scan_mutation_closure.py is committed and re-runnable from this repository's own fixture alone, no external fetch or local CPP clone required, so the sentence and its removal are reproducible evidence, not merely a one-time claim.

mutation.removed_text:
A
  `skipped gates:` name is a SKIP row and a `zero coverage:` or no-tests name is
  a WARN row - never a PASS.
mutation.diagnose_evidence: evals/calibration-287/evidence/discrimination-mutation-diagnose.json: skillc profile diagnose against both the intact and degraded closures (0 problems, complete, on both - necessary but not sufficient, since removing one prose sentence never breaks a declared reference) PLUS an occurrence scan of the whole installed closure (37 files, per evidence/inventory.json) for the sentence's distinctive phrases, positive-controlled against the intact closure (finds the sentence at reference.md:72-73) before trusting the degraded result (0 hits of 'never a PASS' anywhere; the only other agent-facing hit in reference.md, an unrelated bullet about exit code 4, is present unchanged in both closures). Every other hit, in both closures, is in lib/cicd/runner.py, lib/cicd/steps.py or scripts/flow-finish-gate.sh - shell/Python comments or the literal verdict string flow-finish-gate.sh EMITS, never an interpretive instruction the agent reads, confirming #270's own PROVENANCE.md finding by direct scan rather than by inspection. claim_holds: true.

task._comment: skillc#270 merged (PR #350, flow-check-honest declared; PR #351 re-certified gate-stops-early against its own discrimination/fixture and discrimination/reference trees - the tree THIS declaration's attempts are actually graded against, not only the generic fixture/reference pair). Certification must also produce a case-pairing record (skillc#273) binding an intact attempt and a degraded attempt as a reciprocal pair on this task/grader/subject revision - the #150 non-discriminating-result risk is named explicitly as open until the pilot, per the orchestrator's review on #270 (comment 6025382159).

pre_registered_risks.statement: Two routes in the degraded reference.md survive the mutation and could let the degraded arm reach SKIP without the removed sentence at all, found reading the degraded text directly (not reasoned about in the abstract; see evals/level3/gate-stops-early/PROVENANCE.md's own 'Pre-registered' section for the full citation). (1) '"Read one table row per step id (`lint`, `test`, `typecheck`) from the runner JSON's `step_details`."' - the runner JSON marks a skipped step's own status as skipped regardless of which arm installed the skill, so the agent can report SKIP from the data table alone. (2) the same bullet's '"`FLOW_FINISH_GATE: warn (...)` (exit 3) - repeat the qualification verbatim."' - discrimination/fixture's real verdict line is 'FLOW_FINISH_GATE: warn (skipped gates: typecheck)', so repeating it verbatim echoes the SKIP qualification either way. Neither phrase matches evals/calibration-287/evidence/scan_mutation_closure.py's three scan phrases, which is why that scan correctly did not flag them - it answers whether the specific sentence or an agent-facing copy survives, not whether some other route reaches the same answer.
pre_registered_risks.pre_registered_interpretation: If the pilot shows the degraded arm reporting SKIP at a rate near the intact arm's, these two routes are the leading explanation, and - per P4 - the case returns to design rather than being read as a surprise. This does not change the mutation now: the pilot exists to measure exactly this.

tolerance.rule: max(1, ceil(0.05 * attempts_per_arm)) = max(1, ceil(0.5)) = 1 at n=10 (P5)

test: One-sided Fisher's exact test, H1: P(pass|intact) > P(pass|degraded), alpha 0.05, over evaluable attempts (claude-power-pack#1084 comment 6014163660, cited verbatim in skillc#287 comment 6014179807) - NOT run on this pilot's data (no_verdict_statement above); this field documents the MAIN study's test for cross-reference, since the pilot exists to size it.
